Data Source Facts Label
1. Source Identity
Source name Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) 7
Domain/topic Health and healthcare experience
Source type Federally funded public-use dataset
2. Collection Context
Collector/producer The survey is administered by the National Cancer Institute, a public federal agency (part of NIH) and carried out by Westat, a private research corporation
Original purpose To collect nationally representative data on the American public's access to and use of health information, in order to improve health communication
Collection method Mail survey; households got mailed a questionnaire and one adult filled it out themselves either on paper or online
Record-creation event A sampled adult completes and returns the survey either by paper (mail) or online
3. Observation and Scope
Unit of observation One adult's survey response. Each row is one person's answers about their health status, healthcare experiences, and background
Population or objects represented Civilian, non-institutionalized adults (18+) living in the US
Time period covered March 25 - Sept 16, 2024
Geographic area coverage United States (national)
4. Variables and Data Structure
Main variables/fields Chronic conditions/Health Status (MedConditions_Diabetes, MedConditions_HighBP, MedConditions_HeartCondition, MedConditions_LungDisease, EverHadCancer, GeneralHealth) Provider communication (ChanceAskQuestions, ExplainedClearly, SpentEnoughTime, InvolvedDecisions) Quality and trust (QualityCare, TrustHCSystem, DiscriminatedMedCare2) Care coordination (ManageMultipleProviders, ProbCare_WaitLong2, ProbCare_RedoTest) Access/Cost (HealthInsurance2, FreqGoProvider, DiffPayMedBills) Demographics (Age, BirthSex, RaceEthn5, Education, IncomeRanges)
Data types included Primarily categorical (yes/no), rating scales (never/sometimes/usually/always), a few numeric (age, height, weight), and IDs (anonymous household ID)
Direct measurements Age, height, weight, education, household income range, whether they have health insurance (yes/no), number of provider visits in past year. All responses are self reported by respondent (not measured or verified)
Possible proxy variables "Has a doctor ever told you that you had..." questions (MedConditions columns and EverHadCancer) may stand in for actually having the condition. Self-rated health (GeneralHealth) may stand in for actual health status. Care quality and provider communication ratings (QualityCare, SpentEnoughTime, ExplainedClearly, InvolvedDecisions) may stand in for the actual quality of care received. Trust in healthcare system (TrustHCSystem) may stand in for past experiences with it. Number of provider visits (FreqGoProvider), health insurance status (HealthInsurance2), and difficulty paying medical bills (DiffPayMedBills) may stand in for access to care
5. Documentation
Documentation found Methodology Report, Public Codebook, Survey Overview and Data Analysis Recommendations, History Document, Annotated Questionnaire
Stated collection details 36k addresses were randomly selected from a national list of home addresses. Addresses were sorted into four groups (urban/rural and high/low minority population) and more were purposely picked from high minority and rural areas. One adult per household was chosen using the next birthday method. Households got up to 5 mailings, with $2 sent to everyone and larger payments offered to some. 7,585 surveys came back, and blank/incomplete/duplicates were dropped which left 7,278 (Response rate was ~27%). Returned paper surveys were scanned and web surveys were exported, then both were checked, cleaned, and combined into one dataset
